text:
alex: quick heads-up — found a reproducible issue in the Node sampleapp: x-request-id disappears when our recommended fetch-retry triggers a retry. short repro below.

maria: that will break joins in tracing dashboards. is this only happening with fetch-retry?

taylor: probably an OTEL hook ordering + Request clone issue. some retry libs create a new Request and the headers aren't copied.

alex: repro (very small):
```js
// repro.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const retry = require('fetch-retry')(fetch);
await retry('https://internal/generate', { retries: 1, headers: { 'x-request-id': 'rid-900' } });
```

alex: trimmed logs show initial outgoing with id, then retry outgoing with id missing: 
2024-10-01T08:12:01Z sampleapp DEBUG http.outgoing x-request-id=rid-900
2024-10-01T08:12:02Z sampleapp DEBUG http.outgoing x-request-id=-

kevin: can we re-inject from AsyncLocalStorage in our OTEL http hook as a mitigation? only for allowlisted headers (x-request-id, traceparent). do not touch Authorization.

taylor: agree. ALS injection + allowlist is minimal and backward-compatible. also add an e2e that simulates a 502 and asserts header preserved across retry.

maria: add note to quickstart about the fetch-retry caveat until the sampleapp patch ships.

alex: I'll open a PR with a small middleware (store incoming id in ALS) and a test.

telemetry-bot: Created issue #4377: "Node sampleapp: x-request-id lost across fetch-retry; add ALS reinjection + e2e" (assigned devex).

kevin: also flag for parity — run same check against Go and Python sampleapps. alex can run quick smoke tomorrow.
